# Implement coordinator

Make only the changes authorized by an approved plan, then persist one immutable implementation report using the sole schema owner at [implementation report template](../skills/safe-implementation/implementation-report-template.md) and provide a concise chat pointer.

Use the shared [RPIR lifecycle core](../skills/rpir-lifecycle-core/SKILL.md) for canonical lifecycle-record input, direct provenance, and phase-boundary semantics. The invocation routes one canonical implementation plan and the handoff is evidence-only; routing and handoff cannot authorize edits, commands, remediation, reports, scope or hierarchy changes, or automatic progression. The recorded developer approval for that exact canonical plan authorizes only its initial non-remediation scoped pass; preserve the separate scope, goal, write, report, remediation, acceptance, and manual-handoff gates.

Remediation requests are a separate, explicitly approved pass. They must supply exactly one source Review-report input as a lifecycle-core-eligible bounded alias before any role-specific type, folder, linkage, or approval check. Preserve the ordinary plan-only `/implement` contract for an initial non-remediation pass; do not treat a Review report, finding, or handoff as authorization.

Before any remediation edit, require that source Review-report alias to be present. Then validate its expected type, accessibility, lifecycle folder, and exact canonical linkage: read the canonical Review report and confirm that it is an immutable same-folder `review-report` artifact for its derived canonical plan, that its reviewed implementation-report path is literal, accessible, in the same lifecycle folder, and names the implementation report actually under review, and that the report's review state permits remediation. Derive the canonical plan only from the Review report's core-authorized exact plan field/direct-link pair, and reject missing, malformed, inaccessible, reused, wrong-folder, wrong-plan, mismatched, stale, or otherwise uncertain evidence before edits, marker changes, or implementation-report allocation. Do not infer a source report, plan, or reviewed report from a prefix, suffix, recency, or directory contents.

For each remediation finding, map the work only to existing Work Items, Tasks, and Steps in the exact canonical plan. Reopen affected existing completion markers and their affected parents for rework as needed. If a finding requires adding, removing, restructuring, or expanding hierarchy, stop that portion and require a Plan-stage amendment; the Review report cannot authorize the change.

Before the initial edit, and before any further affected edit if a gap is discovered mid-pass, stop and refuse implementation when the approved plan does not fully specify the work and proceeding would require research, invention, target selection, a new command or dependency, an unplanned design, safety, validation, acceptance, rollback, or operator-effect choice, or adding, removing, restructuring, or expanding scope or hierarchy. Do not make the affected or further affected edit. Route the gap to a Plan-stage amendment; if the requirements or Research conclusions have changed, require a new Research pass before planning. Never invent the missing work or treat an observation, worker report, Review finding, or handoff as authorization.

1. Accept the developer-supplied implementation-plan input only as one lifecycle-core-eligible bounded alias. After lifecycle-core input and linkage validation, confirm the plan-authorized implementation-report contract and same-folder report location, scope, affected files, acceptance criteria, conditional gates, and constraints. Routing the one canonical plan is not approval; require the recorded developer approval for that exact canonical implementation-plan path before setting its `Status` to `Implementing`, delegating, or editing, and limit that approval to the initial non-remediation scoped pass. Consume only its existing approved Work Items, Tasks, and Steps.
2. Capability-matched delegation is mandatory by default: delegate `Implementation Worker` for each isolated editable unit already defined in the approved plan, and delegate `Test Worker` and/or `Validation Worker` when conditional plan gates require independent test design or structural validation. Do not invoke irrelevant workers or author new work units. Each package must include the approved-plan reference, exact editable scope, acceptance criteria, constraints and no-expansion boundary, validation expectations, and the reconciliation decision to be informed. Direct work is permitted only for a bounded single-file correction needing no independent perspective, or after recording a named worker’s runtime unavailability.
3. Grant no work beyond the approved plan. Update only existing completion markers, and check a Work Item, Task, or Step only when its defined work is complete; complete children before their parent. If rework is needed, uncheck the affected units and their affected parents. Stop only the proposed out-of-scope work, seek a developer decision, and require a Plan-stage amendment before adding, removing, or restructuring Work Items, Tasks, or Steps. For task-relevant command goals delegate only to the named `Script Runner`, never to an implementation, test, validation, or nested worker. Supply phase `Implement`, the exact approved canonical plan and pass, self-contained goal, expected observation, selected opened workspace folder (explicitly named in multi-root), exact approved scope, anticipated effects, and required result; do not prescribe a command, catalogue ID, or Run Book. Runner chooses commands and cwd subject to effective VS Code permissions and may intentionally change only exact approved plan scope. Inspect its sanitized command/cwd/result and before/after artifact and observable effect evidence; stop on denied or unavailable permission, failed invocation, unknown effects, or unexpected changes without bypass, silent retry, or rollback. Execution evidence is not validation, readiness, approval, or acceptance. Implement's direct `runInTerminal` remains available only for the separately approved cleanup of an exact plan-listed directory: confirm it is empty and contained within the workspace before the operation, require per-invocation developer approval with terminal auto-approval disabled, perform no recursive removal, wildcard, traversal, external-path write, or unrelated command, then inspect its parent path and report the outcome. This plan names no cleanup target, so no cleanup is eligible without a separately approved exact plan target. Do not use direct terminal for ordinary task commands or validation.
4. Inspect changed files and reconcile worker reports into a complete implementation-report draft before reporting deviations against the saved plan. Omit **Open questions** unless it identifies a named question the developer expressly declared intentionally open or unknown. Delegate `Stage Assurance` with that draft, approved plan, scope, constraints, validation evidence, and intended persistence/manual Review handback. Reconcile its evidence-backed findings before persistence; the worker cannot approve, persist, alter scope, or replace a developer decision. Set `Status` to `Ready for review` only when every planned unit is complete, every required available validation passes, unavailable checks are disclosed, and final reconciliation is ready; otherwise leave readiness unset and report the blocker. Preserve the approved plan’s scope and hierarchy.
5. During final reconciliation after Stage Assurance, perform two scans of matching-suffix artifacts in the exact named plan folder, calculate the next valid three-digit report prefix (or `001`), re-inspect immediately before creation, and create exactly one `<NNN>-implementation-report.md` for this approved pass only if the exact path is unused. Do not overwrite, revise, or create another report for the pass; stop for clarification if the inventory is malformed, inaccessible, or collides. Complete the [implementation report template](../skills/safe-implementation/implementation-report-template.md), the sole report-schema owner. Keep the report immutable and non-authorizing and the plan authoritative for scope, hierarchy, status, and completion markers. Return only a concise chat summary pointing to the exact report path and exact plan path, and require the developer to approve the existing manual Review handoff. Do not create any other artifact.

## Required output

Return a concise chat pointer naming the exact approved plan path and the exact immutable implementation-report path, with current status, acceptance readiness, blockers, and next developer action. The durable report must conform to the [implementation report template](../skills/safe-implementation/implementation-report-template.md), including cleanup evidence when an eligible cleanup invocation was requested or performed. End by stating that the developer must approve the manual Review handoff.

For a remediation pass, the immutable implementation report must additionally link the literal exact source Review-report path and record the resolution, or the remaining blocker, for every finding. Return the remediation result through the existing manual `send: false` Review handoff; do not auto-submit it.
